title: Nonnegative component energy
statement: Let $\Omega$ and $\iota$ be finite nonempty sets, let $\pi$ be a probability mass function on $\Omega$, and let $(\psi_a)_{a\in\iota}$ be a basis of real-valued functions on $\Omega$ that contains the constant-one function and is orthonormal for the inner product weighted by $\pi$. For any $n\in\mathbb N$, any real-valued function $f$ on $\Omega^n$, and any set of coordinates $S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$, the squared norm of the Fourier component of $f$ supported on $S$, with respect to the product probability measure $\pi^n$, is nonnegative.
hypotheses_covered: Basis is orthonormal for the $\pi$-weighted inner product
